metric_model: CHAOSS AI Alignment - Community Governed Use

scope.note: Scoring confined to the files named on the command line; 'no' means not addressed in those files.

domains.scope_or_volume_limits: AI-generated code only permitted for accepted issues; forbidden for issues labeled 'good first issue'; drive-by PRs without an accepted issue will be closed

evidence.quote: All AI usage in any form must be disclosed.
Pull requests with AI-generated code can only be for accepted issues.
AI may not be used for issues marked as "good first issue".
AI-generated code must have been fully verified with human use.
Issues and discussions can use AI assistance but must have a full human-in-the-loop.

domains.suggested_improvement: no accountability holder named for AI-assisted contributions
domains.reasoning: Policy states clear supervision (human-in-the-loop, disclosure, verification) and scope limits (accepted issues only, no good-first-issue) for PRs/issues/comments, but never states who is answerable for the resulting content - only that maintainers may close non-compliant PRs, which is enforcement, not accountability.

domains.suggested_improvement: no mention of meeting/notetaker bots at all
domains.reasoning: The document never discusses recorded meetings, transcription, or notetaker bots in any form.

domains.scope_or_volume_limits: applies to non-code media/text: art, images, videos, audio, etc.

evidence.quote: No AI-generated media or text (other than code) is allowed (art, images, videos, audio, etc.).

domains.suggested_improvement: no accountability holder named for banned-content rule
domains.reasoning: A clear ban is stated for non-code AI-generated content (documentation prose, art, media), but no one is named as accountable for compliance or violation - only the prohibition itself, enforced implicitly by maintainers.

domains.rationale_only_mention: we have experienced an increasing number of low-quality pull requests that consume significant amounts of human reviewers' time
domains.suggested_improvement: no rule on AI use in moderation actions; no supervision level
domains.reasoning: The policy cites reviewer time burden as a rationale for its rules (moderation load, per the metric's own carve-out), but it never states a rule about whether or how AI may be used to perform moderation actions (e.g. auto-closing, labeling). The closing of non-compliant PRs is a maintainer enforcement action, not an AI moderation capability being addressed.

domains.suggested_improvement: no rule on humans using AI tools to review contributions
domains.reasoning: The only mention of 'code reviews' is in the context of agents being forbidden from posting them autonomously, which is scored under autonomous use per the metric's own instruction. No statement addresses a human reviewer's own use of AI tooling to assist in reviewing a contribution.

domains.scope_or_volume_limits: covers posting issues, making pull requests, posting comments, posting code reviews, adding reactions, and any other repository interaction

evidence.quote: Agents are strictly forbidden from interacting with our repository.
Any interaction on our repository must be done by a human.

domains.suggested_improvement: no accountability holder named for the autonomous-agent ban
domains.reasoning: A comprehensive ban on autonomous agent interaction is stated with broad scope, but no party is named as accountable for enforcement failures or for supervising compliance - the rule only obliges that humans do the interacting.

domains.suggested_improvement: no mention of energy, water, or carbon impact
domains.reasoning: The rationale section discusses reviewer time and low-quality PRs, not energy or water use; environmental impact is never raised anywhere in the document.

domains.suggested_improvement: no mention of server load or hardware cost
domains.reasoning: No statement in the policy discusses server load, hardware financing, or infrastructure costs related to AI use.

domains.suggested_improvement: no mention of project data being used to train models
domains.reasoning: The document does not discuss whether Polars' own issues, discussions, code, or user data may be used to train AI models; its concerns are about AI output quality and disclosure, not about the project's data feeding models.

consent_policy_specificity.overall_posture: Polars' AI policy is detailed and restrictive for code contributions and non-code content (banning autonomous agents, non-code AI media, and requiring disclosure plus human-in-the-loop verification for AI-assisted code/issues), but it never names an accountability holder for any domain and is entirely silent on notetaker bots, review-tool use by humans, moderation actions, environmental impact, infrastructure strain, and training data use.

awaiting_implementation.specific_tools_in_use: Awaiting implementation: named-product detection beyond known file signatures
awaiting_implementation.ai_tool_owner: Awaiting implementation: ownership and data control
awaiting_implementation.environmental_footprint: Awaiting implementation: model/system card and ESG disclosure
awaiting_implementation.proportionality: Awaiting implementation: resource use relative to contributor count (needs platform usage data)

use_composition_partial.note: Detection only. Absence of signal is not absence of use.

policy_change.blocker: Draft classifier not wired in or validated against hand-graded history. Repo.history() and Repo.commit_patch() supply the diffs.

use_compliance.blocker: Derived metric. Requires disclosed-use data (Use Composition) checked against the specificity grid. Composition is only partially detectable, so the comparison is not yet sound.

misuse.blocker: Not automatable. CHAOSS marks the core signals unknown: text-based AI detectors are unreliable, and license-laundering and wrongful-accusation incidents need maintainer self-report.
